    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
        else . end)) as $knobs |
    {
      schema_version: 1,
      id: $id,
      profile: $sel.name,
      profile_source: $sel.source,
      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
      profile_keys: $keys,
      knobs: $knobs,
      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
  local w
  while IFS= read -r w; do
    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
  return 0
}

_loa_pl_write_cache() {
  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  fi
  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  else
    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  fi
  return 0
}

# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
_loa_pl_load() {
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
    local j
    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  _loa_pl_build || return 1
  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
  _loa_pl_write_cache
  return 0
}

# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
_loa_pl_live() {
  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
  return 0
}

loa_profile() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
  else
    echo standard
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_source() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
  else
    echo default
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_overrides() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_effective_json() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
  else
    echo '{}'
  fi
  return 0
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
  export LC_ALL=C
  case "${1:-}" in
    profile)   loa_profile ;;
    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
# DEC-0141).
#
# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
# PER TASK:
#
#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
#
# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
#
# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
# file is not written through.
#
# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
#
# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
# full each time and those caches are gone.

set -uo pipefail
umask 077
export LC_ALL=C

_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0

# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
case "$switch" in
    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
esac
THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))

# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
payload="$(cat)"
[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
            else 1 end;
    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    select(type == "object") |
    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    ([($tn | tojson),
      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
       else 0 end | tostring),
      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
      (now | todate)] | .[])
' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
{
    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
    IFS= read -r LINES
    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
    IFS= read -r TS
} <<< "$fields"
case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
    *) exit 0 ;;
esac
[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0

# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
    local s
    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}
payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"

task_raw=""
if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
fi
KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"

# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi

# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0

PRIOR=0
if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
fi
RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))

printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
n=0
while IFS= read -r old; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)

# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
OVER=false
(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    else
        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    fi
fi

# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2

    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

exit 0
=====
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
#
# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
#
# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
#
# No floor key may appear here. The floor config keys are listed once, in
# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
# the key would not discriminate between profiles.
schema_version: 1

profiles:
  lean:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: false
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: false
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: false
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  standard:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  full:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: true
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: true
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: true

# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
# file is not written through.
#
# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
#
# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
# full each time and those caches are gone.

set -uo pipefail
umask 077
export LC_ALL=C

_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0

# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
case "$switch" in
    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
esac
THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))

# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
payload="$(cat)"
[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
            else 1 end;
    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    select(type == "object") |
    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    ([($tn | tojson),
      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
       else 0 end | tostring),
      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
      (now | todate)] | .[])
' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
{
    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
    IFS= read -r LINES
    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
    IFS= read -r TS
} <<< "$fields"
case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
    *) exit 0 ;;
esac
[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0

# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
    local s
    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}
payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"

task_raw=""
if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
fi
KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"

# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi

# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0

PRIOR=0
if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
fi
RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))

printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
n=0
while IFS= read -r old; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)

# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
OVER=false
(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    else
        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    fi
fi

# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2

    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

exit 0
=====
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
#
# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
#
# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
#

# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
# the key would not discriminate between profiles.
schema_version: 1

profiles:
  lean:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: false
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: false
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: false
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  standard:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  full:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: true
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: true
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: true

new file mode 100755
index 00000000..00fedec5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/check-knob-readers.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
  return 0
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# jq presence probe (SDD §6.5 — SKP-008 mitigation, not full fix).
# If jq is absent, the input parse on line ~120 returns empty → existing
# fail-open guard exits 0. v1.38.0 adds a one-shot stderr WARNING so the
# operator / agent sees the safety guard is disabled this session.
# Tracked as cycle-112 candidate (filesystem-marker variant for cross-
# invocation persistence; env-var doesn't propagate across hook subprocess
# invocations per Flatline SKP-002 round-3 finding).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# perf pass-11 (skill-loop, 2026-07-06): HIGH-002 fix (BB review of PR #1176).
# Passes 2 & 8 introduced bash-4-only constructs into this fence (${x,,}
# case-folding, `mapfile`); pre-loop it was bash-3.2-portable (echo|grep -i).
# macOS ships bash 3.2. This guard runs BEFORE any bash-4 expansion executes
# (bash 3.2 defers ${,,} validation and the mapfile builtin lookup to runtime,
# so a runtime guard at the first executable line runs first and never reaches
# them). If a bash >=4 exists (the framework already requires it — beads-health
# etc. source bash-version-guard.sh), re-exec under it; stdin (the hook payload)
# and argv survive exec. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED (exit 2 = block): a
# destructive-command fence must never silently allow when it cannot evaluate.
# The generic bash-version-guard.sh exits 1, which is a NON-blocking PreToolUse
# hook error (fail-OPEN) — wrong direction for this hook, hence the inline form.
if [ "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}" -lt 4 ]; then
    for _bh_cand in /opt/homebrew/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/bash /usr/bin/bash bash; do
        if command -v "$_bh_cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            _bh_major="$("$_bh_cand" -c 'echo "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}"' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
            if [ "${_bh_major:-0}" -ge 4 ]; then exec "$_bh_cand" "$0" "$@"; fi
        fi
    done
    echo "[block-destructive-bash] BLOCKED: bash >=4 required to evaluate the destructive-command fence (found ${BASH_VERSION:-unknown}); refusing to run degraded rather than allow a command unchecked. Install bash>=4 (macOS: brew install bash)." >&2
    exit 2
fi

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [[ -z "${LOA_BLOCK_DESTRUCTIVE_JQ_MISSING_WARNED:-}" ]]; then
    echo "WARNING: block-destructive-bash: jq not in PATH — destructive-command pattern matching is DISABLED for this session. Install jq to restore safety guards." >&2

# so a runtime guard at the first executable line runs first and never reaches
# them). If a bash >=4 exists (the framework already requires it — beads-health
# etc. source bash-version-guard.sh), re-exec under it; stdin (the hook payload)
# and argv survive exec. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED (exit 2 = block): a
# destructive-command fence must never silently allow when it cannot evaluate.
# The generic bash-version-guard.sh exits 1, which is a NON-blocking PreToolUse
# hook error (fail-OPEN) — wrong direction for this hook, hence the inline form.
if [ "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}" -lt 4 ]; then
    for _bh_cand in /opt/homebrew/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/bash /usr/bin/bash bash; do
        if command -v "$_bh_cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            _bh_major="$("$_bh_cand" -c 'echo "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}"' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
            if [ "${_bh_major:-0}" -ge 4 ]; then exec "$_bh_cand" "$0" "$@"; fi
        fi
    done
    echo "[block-destructive-bash] BLOCKED: bash >=4 required to evaluate the destructive-command fence (found ${BASH_VERSION:-unknown}); refusing to run degraded rather than allow a command unchecked. Install bash>=4 (macOS: brew install bash)." >&2
    exit 2

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run-corpus.sh — replay tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl through the
# block-destructive-bash hook and summarise (cycle-125 Sprint 1, PRD FR-1).
#
# Usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]
# Each row: {id, cmd, expect: allow|block|residual, rule, why, cwd: repo|tmp, env?: {TMPDIR}}
#   allow    → benign: the hook must exit 0
#   block    → dangerous: the hook must exit 2
#   residual → accepted false positive: counted, never gated
# --knob-off  writes destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false into the
#             replay root's .loa.config.yaml (cycle-129 FR-6: the pre-cycle scan);
#             compare it with the pre-change hook through --rows.
# --rows      prints "<id> <exit code>" per row instead of the summary (for diffs).
# Output (text): one line per mismatch, then
#   "benign P/T dangerous B/T residual R/T runtime_ms N p95_ms M";
# --json prints {benign_pass, benign_total, dangerous_block, dangerous_total,
#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, p95_ms, rows, mismatches: [..]}.
# p95_ms is the 95th percentile of the per-row hook wall time (the hook process
# only; the jq row parsing is outside the timed span).
set -uo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
hook="$root/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
corpus="$root/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl"
json=0 knob_off=0 rows_out=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --hook) hook="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --corpus) corpus="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) json=1; shift ;;
    --knob-off) knob_off=1; shift ;;
    --rows) rows_out=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
[[ -x "$hook" || -f "$hook" ]] || { echo "hook not found: $hook" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$corpus" ]] || { echo "corpus not found: $corpus" >&2; exit 2; }

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
repo="$work/repo"; scratch="$work/scratch"
mkdir -p "$repo" "$scratch"
export LOA_REPO_ROOT="$work"
export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1   # audit rows this replay writes carry replay: true (cycle-129 DEC-0167)
if (( knob_off )); then
  printf 'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false\n' > "$work/.loa.config.yaml"
fi

bp=0 bt=0 db=0 dt=0 rp=0 rt=0
mismatches=()
durations=()
# Microsecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
now_us() {
  if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
    local s="${EPOCHREALTIME%.*}" us="${EPOCHREALTIME#*.}"
    echo $(( s * 1000000 + 10#${us:0:6} ))
  else
    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000 ))
  fi
}

# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

The review gate returned CHANGES_REQUIRED, not "All good". Every counted finding below was re-derived from `pr/head/`; the security findings were reproduced against both the head hook and the base hook from `pr/base/`.

## Executive Summary

Most of this sprint holds up when executed, not just read. The fence corpus passes in full with the classifier on, and the knob-off run reproduces exactly the documented pre-change misses. The profile resolver, the lint invariants and the implement-gate mode matrix are green. Floor keys stay out of reach of the profile mechanism.

One finding blocks the merge. The new heredoc consumer classifier, described by the PR as fail-closed, fails open for a heredoc whose target file is executed later in the same Bash command through a substitution, a pipe into a shell, a variable, a glob or an argument-passing wrapper. The base fence blocks these commands and the head fence allows them. Turning the classifier knob off restores the block, so the regression is introduced by this change. Its blast radius is the System Zone write protection, which is a floor guard.

Five medium findings follow: the classifier's body keep-list and destination test are not conservative, two jq 1.6 portability failures in `run-checkpoint.sh`, the guardrail default flip that also fails open when the profile library is unavailable, and a roughly 5x to 9x latency increase in the per-write karpathy hook.

**Overall Risk Level:** HIGH

## Scope and method

- Read the implementation of every touched script under `pr/head/`: the fence classifier, `implement-gate.sh`, `run-checkpoint.sh`, `profile-lib.sh`, the karpathy hook, the two guardrail scripts, `loa-status.sh`, the surface hooks, `lint-invariants.sh`, `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`, the two new tools, and the config, profile and floor data.
- Executed from a copy of the head tree under `$HOME` because the sandbox mounts `/tmp` noexec and strips exec bits. Ran the fence corpus with the knob on and off, the head and base hooks on hand-built payloads, the PR's bats suites under jq 1.6 and jq 1.7.1, and a per-write latency measurement.
- `security-audit-scope.sh` reports 0 sources and 0 sinks for this shell repository. The recon was done by hand. The untrusted inputs are the Bash command text (fence), the Write/Edit payload and `.run/` files (gate), `.loa.config.yaml` and `.run/effective-config.json` (profile-lib), and feedback files plus the ledger (run-checkpoint).
- Phase 1C ran: `adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id sprint-1 --diff-file pr/head.diff --json` finished with exit 0.

| Check on the head tree | Result |
|------------------------|--------|
| Fence corpus, classifier on | benign 89/89, dangerous 142/142, p95 76 ms |
| Fence corpus, knob off | misses only D122, D123, D127, D131, D136, D141; blocks B80, B82, B85, B87, B88 |
| `profile-lib.bats` | 17/17 |
| `lint-invariants.bats` | 9/9 |
| `implement-gate.bats` IG-9 to IG-33 | pass (IG-1 to IG-8 and IG-12 need fixtures outside the PR) |
| `run-checkpoint-derive.bats` / `-record-round.bats`, jq 1.7.1 | 22/22, 8/8 |
| Same suites, jq 1.6 | 18 of 22 and 1 of 8 fail (MEDIUM-2, MEDIUM-3) |

---

## Findings

### HIGH-1 — The heredoc classifier drops a body that the same command executes

- **Severity:** high · **Confidence:** high · **Category:** security, protection-mechanism failure
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-631` (`_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`), with the replacement of the full scan at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:1063`
- **CWE-693** Protection Mechanism Failure: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html
- **CWE-184** Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

Vulnerable code, `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:625` and `:631`:

```bash
u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
...
if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
```

The header at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:154-156` claims that a target named anywhere else in the command outside a safe reader makes the heredoc interpreter-class. The code compares each token for exact equality with the basename, then judges only the segment holding that token. A consumer that reaches the file inside a substitution, through a pipe whose reader is `cat`, through a variable or glob, or through an argument-passing wrapper never satisfies both tests. The heredoc stays non-executing, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` drops every body segment except fence verbs. A System-Zone write or a destructive command in the body is removed before the FR-SZ and FR-2 rules run.

Reproduction: for each consumer shape the base hook exits 2 (FR-SZ2-COPY or FR-2) and the head hook exits 0. With `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false` the head hook blocks again. Direct consumers such as `bash <file>` and `./<file>` are still caught. The documented gap at `head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:298` covers a *later* command only, while these run inside one Bash tool call. The review and both dissent voices found the same defect independently.

**Required fix:**
1. When a later line names the target, treat the heredoc as interpreter-class if that line holds any substitution or process-substitution opener, a pipe into an interpreter or wrapper, a glob, or a variable bound to the target. Match by substring, not token equality, in those cases.
2. Treat a pipeline whose downstream member is an interpreter or wrapper as executing its input, whichever member names the target.
3. Add the reproduced shapes to `tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl` as `expect: block` rows and rerun the corpus with the knob on and off.

### MEDIUM-1 — Body keep-list and destination test are not conservative

- **Severity:** medium · **Confidence:** high · **Category:** security
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214-219`, `:538-574`, `:303-322`
- **CWE-184:** https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

Three gaps make any missed execution path worse than one dropped line:

- `_bdb_hd_is_destructive` keeps only the FR-2 family of verbs. The verbs the floor FR-SZ rules match, such as copy, move, link, tee and in-place sed, are not kept, so those rules never see a System-Zone write inside a kept body.
- `_bdb_hd_segword` does not strip shell keywords, leading redirects or `trap`, so a fence verb after one of them is dropped. A reproduced keyword-prefixed body is blocked by the base hook and allowed by the head hook when it is executed in the same command.
- `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` matches the target path literally at `:311` without collapsing `..`, `//` or `/./`. A git hook path written with a `..` segment is therefore not recognised as executable content. Combined with the keep-list gap, the dissent's same-command git-hook shape reproduces as allowed on head and blocked on base.

**Fix:** keep the FR-SZ verbs, and any segment that names `.claude/` or `.git/`. Skip shell keywords, redirects and `trap` in `_bdb_hd_segword`, or fall back to the full scan when a segment starts with one. Normalise the destination before matching. Add corpus rows for each case.

### MEDIUM-2 — `run-checkpoint.sh derive` does not compile on jq 1.6

- **Severity:** medium · **Confidence:** high · **Category:** code quality, portability
- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378`
- **CWE-758** Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/758.html

`--arg label "$label"` binds `$label`, and `label` is a jq keyword. jq 1.6 rejects the program (verified: `$label REJECTED` on 1.6, accepted on 1.7.1). Under `set -e`, `derive`, `mark` and the refresh after each checkpoint `write` therefore fail on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 hosts. The file-authoritative run position (FR-5) never gets written there, and the deny mode of the implement gate falls back to an unknown position. 18 of 22 derive cases fail on jq 1.6.

**Fix:** rename the binding, for example `--arg lbl`, or state and probe a jq 1.7 floor.

### MEDIUM-3 — An empty trailer aborts `fb_parse` on jq 1.6

- **Severity:** medium · **Confidence:** high · **Category:** code quality, portability
- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226`
- **CWE-754** Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

```bash
jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
```

jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input (1.7.1 exits 4, verified), so a feedback file without a `LOA-VERDICT` trailer leaves `$pj` empty, `--argjson p ''` fails and `record-round` aborts. The circuit breaker then misses that round. RCR-7 fails on jq 1.6.

**Fix:** test `[[ -n "$pj" ]]` before the jq check, and do the same for `$vj`.

- **Severity:** medium · **Confidence:** medium · **Category:** security configuration
- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh:138-141`, `head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:40-41`
- **CWE-1188** Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1188.html
- **CWE-636** Not Failing Securely: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/636.html

```bash
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh"
...
    enforce=$(loa_knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce false)
```

Installs without an explicit key move from enforced (the old `// true` and `return 0`) to off under `standard`. The decision is recorded as DEC-0161, but nothing at runtime announces it. The `/loa` Profile line lists explicit overrides only. In addition, the old code fell back to `true` when yq failed. The new code falls back to `false`, and the unguarded `source` under `set -euo pipefail` aborts the script if the library is missing, which the orchestrator treats as fail-open. The same pattern applies to `guardrails.input.enabled` in `guardrails-orchestrator.sh`.

**Fix:** keep the intended default, but fail toward enforcement when resolution is impossible (`|| enforce=true`, guarded `source`). Emit a one-time notice when the effective value differs from the pre-cycle default.

- **Severity:** medium · **Confidence:** medium · **Category:** performance
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131`, with the knob reads at `:74` and `:78`

The PostToolUse hook now forks `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` on every Write, Edit and NotebookEdit. That costs several jq calls, plus `br show` when beads is installed. Two knob resolutions through `profile-lib.sh` add to it.

| Hook, five writes averaged | ms per write |
|----------------------------|--------------|
| base | 28 |
| head, no checkpoint | 152 |
| head, with a checkpoint | 260 |

**Fix:** read `.checkpoint.task` and `.checkpoint.sprint` from the state file with one jq, and resolve both knobs in one call.

- **Severity:** low · **Confidence:** high
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:732-734`, `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1243`

Both comments say that turning `heredoc_classifier` off "only tightens". The corpus shows knob-off misses six dangerous rows that the classifier catches, so the knob is a rollback, not a tightening. The config path falls back to `.` and so follows the process cwd, the same concern `implement-gate.sh` already handles by resolving from its own location. CWE-1188: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1188.html

- **Severity:** low · **Confidence:** medium
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:590`

`LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1` is new in this PR (no occurrence in the base file). It allows every App-Zone write in every mode, including `deny`. The fence states the opposite stance for itself at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:760-761`. The variable is operator-set and logged, so the risk is low. Restricting it to `ask` and `telemetry`, or reading it from outside the repository, would keep `deny` a fence. CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html

- **Severity:** low · **Confidence:** high
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:545-550`

`.run/implement-active.json` sanctions App-Zone writes for two hours, and nothing ties it to the harness. The Write tool path asks, but a Bash write does not. `head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:273` documents this as the accepted gap bead bd-taee, and the repository stays on `ask`, so this is counted low. Before `deny` is promoted to a default, the marker needs integrity, for example an HMAC with a key held outside the tree. CWE-345 Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html

- **Severity:** low · **Confidence:** medium
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303-322`

- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:230`

Most of this sprint holds up when executed, not just read. The fence corpus passes in full with the classifier on, and the knob-off run reproduces exactly the documented pre-change misses. - **CWE-184** Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

```bash
u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
...
if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
```

The header at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:154-156` claims that a target named anywhere else in the command outside a safe reader makes the heredoc interpreter-class. The code compares each token for exact equality with the basename, then judges only the segment holding that token. A consumer that reaches the file inside a substitution, through a pipe whose reader is `cat`, through a variable or glob, or through an argument-passing wrapper never satisfies both tests. The heredoc stays non-executing, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` drops every body segment except fence verbs. A System-Zone write or a destructive command in the body is removed before the FR-SZ and FR-2 rules run.

Reproduction: for each consumer shape the base hook exits 2 (FR-SZ2-COPY or FR-2) and the head hook exits 0. With `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false` the head hook blocks again. Direct consumers such as `bash <file>` and `./<file>` are still caught. The documented gap at `head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:298` covers a *later* command only, while these run inside one Bash tool call. The review and both dissent voices found the same defect independently.

**Required fix:**
1. When a later line names the target, treat the heredoc as interpreter-class if that line holds any substitution or process-substitution opener, a pipe into an interpreter or wrapper, a glob, or a variable bound to the target. Match by substring, not token equality, in those cases.
2. Treat a pipeline whose downstream member is an interpreter or wrapper as executing its input, whichever member names the target.
3. Add the reproduced shapes to `tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl` as `expect: block` rows and rerun the corpus with the knob on and off.

- **Severity:** medium · **Confidence:** high · **Category:** security
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214-219`, `:538-574`, `:303-322`
- **CWE-184:** https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

Three gaps make any missed execution path worse than one dropped line:

- `_bdb_hd_is_destructive` keeps only the FR-2 family of verbs. The verbs the floor FR-SZ rules match, such as copy, move, link, tee and in-place sed, are not kept, so those rules never see a System-Zone write inside a kept body.

Combined with the keep-list gap, the dissent's same-command git-hook shape reproduces as allowed on head and blocked on base.

**Fix:** keep the FR-SZ verbs, and any segment that names `.claude/` or `.git/`. Skip shell keywords, redirects and `trap` in `_bdb_hd_segword`, or fall back to the full scan when a segment starts with one. Normalise the destination before matching. Add corpus rows for each case.

- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378`
- **CWE-758** Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/758.html

`--arg label "$label"` binds `$label`, and `label` is a jq keyword. jq 1.6 rejects the program (verified: `$label REJECTED` on 1.6, accepted on 1.7.1). **Fix:** rename the binding, for example `--arg lbl`, or state and probe a jq 1.7 floor.

The audit verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The feedback file passes the verdict self-check and is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`. I wrote no COMPLETED marker.

One note on process: the review step returned CHANGES_REQUIRED rather than "All good", so the normal precondition for an audit was not met. I ran the audit anyway because the task said to, and the severity counts decide the verdict.

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 5 |
| Low | 6 |

**The blocker is the heredoc classifier in the Bash safety hook.** It is described as fail-closed, but it fails open when a heredoc's target file is run later in the same command, for example through a substitution, a pipe into a shell, or a variable. I reproduced this against both versions of the hook. The old hook blocks these commands and the new one allows them. Turning the classifier setting off blocks them again, so this change introduced the regression. The exposed protection is the System Zone write guard, which is a floor guard. The finding is at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608`.

**The medium findings:**
- **Classifier lists are too narrow.** The list of commands the classifier keeps from a heredoc body leaves out the System Zone write verbs. Shell keywords hide commands from it, and target paths are not normalised before the check.
- **Run position fails on jq 1.6.** In `run-checkpoint.sh`, `derive` does not compile on jq 1.6 because `$label` is a reserved word there, so the run position is never written on those hosts.
- **Missing trailer breaks the circuit breaker on jq 1.6.** In the same script, a feedback file without a verdict trailer makes `record-round` abort, so that round is not recorded.
- **Guardrails fail open.** The guardrail defaults now resolve to off. If the profile library cannot be loaded, enforcement is skipped instead of applied.
- **The per-write karpathy hook is much slower:**

| Karpathy hook | ms per write |
|---------------|--------------|
| Old version | 28 |
| New version | 152 |
| New version, with a checkpoint | 260 |

The low findings are a wrong comment on the classifier setting and a new environment variable that can override deny mode. The others are a forgeable sanction marker (already a documented accepted gap), an incomplete list of executable destinations, a GNU-only grep, and a thin implementation report with no CHANGELOG entry.

**The two-model adversarial check ran on the diff.** It returned six findings and none were rejected. Five are counted under the findings above. The sixth, about deleted agent-team rules, is not a defect because the rules moved to the agent-teams reference doc.

**Not verified here.** Two of the PR's karpathy test files do not parse in this snapshot, because a secret-redaction pass left a stray quote that also appears in the base file. Two profile-floor tests depend on files or a yq variant outside the PR and need to be confirmed in CI.

**The audit file describes the bypass in prose only.** My first draft listed the exact commands that get past the hook, and a safety filter stopped it. The PR authors will need to rebuild the test cases from the description before adding them to the fence corpus.

I also added a line to `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`.
